name: Galitzenklamm
kurzbeschreibung: The wild Galitzenklamm gorge near Lienz captivates with rushing waterfalls, wooden walkways, via ferratas, and a water playground.
preis: Adults approx. €7.00; discounts for families and guest card holders
oeffnungszeiten: Early May to late October daily from 09:00 to 18:00
beschreibung:
Overview

The dramatically rugged Galitzenklamm gorge lies at the northern foot of the sheer Lienz Dolomites in the municipality of Amlach, just a few kilometers southwest of the sunny town of Lienz in East Tyrol. As a breathtaking natural gorge experience, it has captivated outdoor adventurers, families, and climbers for generations. The foaming waters of the Galitzenbach torrent have carved deeply into the solid limestone rock over millennia, creating roaring cascades, giant glacial potholes, and sculpted rock formations. Boldly engineered timber catwalks, secure stairways, and airy suspension bridges allow visitors to experience the thunder of the elements up close. Today, the Galitzenklamm presents itself as an adventure park with a family water playground, forest ropes course, via ferrata routes, and an interactive stone trail.

Route & Requirements

The tour through the gorge across secure wooden walkways and panoramic platforms takes about 45 to 60 minutes, covering moderate elevation changes. Sturdy, ankle-high hiking shoes with non-slip profile soles and normal walking fitness are required, as the wooden boardwalks can be damp and slippery from waterfall spray. The narrow gorge path is inaccessible for wheelchairs and pushchairs, though the sunny entrance area with the adventure playground is step-free. For climbing enthusiasts, the Galitzenklamm is a true magnet: multiple via ferrata routes, ranging from beginner-friendly paths to the challenging 'Adrenalin' sport via ferrata, traverse directly above the churning canyon (via ferrata kit and helmet mandatory; equipment rental on site).

Visit & Arrival

Galitzenklamm is open daily from early May to late October between 09:00 and 18:00 (until 17:00 in October; closed during severe weather for safety). A modest maintenance fee is charged for admission. Travel by car from Lienz via the B100 Drautalstraße towards Spittal an der Drau or through Amlach (free parking at the entrance). Cyclists can reach the gorge conveniently via the popular Drau Cycle Path R1.

Tips

Stand on the viewing balcony right by the main waterfall to feel the refreshing spray against your skin – a delightful sensation on warm summer days. Conclude your tour with a traditional Tyrolean snack platter in the shaded garden of the rustic Gasthaus Galitzenklamm tavern.
